text:
incident-bot: ALERT: spike in 5xx on serving-cluster-gpupool-1 → detected CUDA error: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS (misaligned device addr). Auto-incident created INC-2024-0713-TRIAGE.
oncall-sre: on it. what nodes are showing the failures and any obvious pattern?
devraj: node gpu-node-7 shows repeated container restarts. kube events show OOM + illegal address from the runtime process.
eli: pulled recent runtime logs:
```
[2024-07-13T11:02:19Z] runtime: ERROR gpu0: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS at loader.c:517
[2024-07-13T11:02:19Z] runtime: trace: kv_cache_evict() -> invalid device pointer during pagewalk
[2024-07-13T11:02:19Z] containerd: ExitCode=137, Killed by OOM
```
morgan: CS: 4 customers reported transient 500s starting ~11:00 UTC. They're on high-throughput embedding routes. Some jobs retried and succeeded.
sre-keenan: any kernel/driver updates recently on that pool?
infra-ops: no driver rollouts in the last 48h. nvidia driver 525.89, kernel 6.1.12. Node was healthy in metrics until 10:58 UTC.
eng-runtime: pattern matches a rare eviction-use-after-free we saw in staging weeks ago when pinned buffer reclamation races with pagewalks under pressure. Could be allocator bug or the kernel NV driver edge-case.
devraj: repro attempt: run sustained high-batch embeddings + concurrent large-context chat; eviction frequency goes up and illegal access reproduces in ~12 minutes.
eli: immediate mitigations we can apply now:
- cordon + drain gpu-node-7
- reduce GPU batch sizes and lower concurrency for the GPU pool
- disable KV prefetch/prefetcher for GPU runtime
- temporarily scale up CPU-only fallback to absorb critical traffic
- if necessary, disable autoscaler bursts to avoid packing too many pods on a single GPU

oncall-sre: executing cordon/drain and enabling fallback. tagging @infra-ops for forensic capture. :rotating_light:
incident-bot: ACTION logged: node gpu-node-7 cordoned at 11:12 UTC by oncall-sre.
infra-ops: starting drain and collecting artifacts: /var/crash, kernel dmesg, nvidia-bug-report, nv-hostengine logs.
devraj: while traffic is moved, pushing a quick runtime config to decrease batch and disable KV prefetch:
```
kubectl -n inference set env ds/serve-runtime KV_PREFETCH=false
kubectl -n inference patch deploy/serve-runtime --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"runtime","env":[{"name":"MAX_GPU_BATCH","value":"8"}]}]}}}}'
```
eng-runtime: config applied. monitoring telemetry for any further CUDA_ILLEGAL events.
eli: saw one final crash from the draining pod with same illegal access stack, then nothing new on other nodes. Good sign.
sre-keenan: likely node-local memory corruption or driver interaction with our runtime allocator. Keep node quarantined.
infra-ops: collected coredumps and syslogs; uploading to /mnt/artifacts/INC-2024-0713-TRIAGE. We recommend reimage for gpu-node-7 after handoff.
eng-runtime: assigning to eng-runtime team to root cause. Initial plan: reproduce with stress harness, enable ASAN/UBSAN in allocator builds, and instrument kv cache eviction paths. Also try to reproduce against a newer driver (528.x) in a test pool.
cs-lead: customer comms: notified affected customers with ETA and mitigation steps. No SLA credit triggers yet but flagged for postmortem.
morgan: impact summary for postmortem: 4 customers experienced short-lived 500s (approx 20–40m window); retries recovered many jobs. No persistent data loss. Severity: Sev2.
eng-runtime: short-term code changes: add pointer checks around GPU buffer references, add guard counters on KV entries, and add exponential backoff for eviction. Filing PRs today.
incident-bot: UPDATE: model-fallback enabled for critical routes at 11:25 UTC to CPU-quantized variants where acceptable.
oncall-sre: handing off to night oncall in 45m. Summary: node gpu-node-7 produced CUDA_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS events -> cordoned & drained -> runtime config tightened (KV_PREFETCH=false, MAX_GPU_BATCH lowered) -> no further illegal events on remaining nodes. Artifacts collected; eng-runtime owns RCA.
eng-runtime: acknowledged. please keep node offline for forensic; will request repro node from infra-ops with matching driver/kernel.
infra-ops: will reimage gpu-node-7 after eng-runtime confirms we captured everything.
cs-lead: will follow up with customers with root-cause when available.
night-sre: taking over monitoring. confirmed receipt.
incident-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: artifacts stored, handoff complete, live mitigation closed. Tags: cuda, illegal_address, eviction, live-mitigation. :white_check_mark:
sre-keenan: thanks everyone — if eng-runtime needs kernel tracing, ping infra-ops for a kernel-trace-enabled repro node.
notes: cordon/drain, runtime config changes, forensic artifacts collected, eng-runtime assigned for RCA
